query: Protocol for deriving expandable skeletal myogenic progenitors and multinucleated myotubes from human pluripotent stem cells
title: Efficient derivation and inducible differentiation of expandable skeletal myogenic cells from human ES and patient-specific iPS cells
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for deriving expandable skeletal myogenic progenitors and multinucleated myotubes from human pluripotent stem cells

### Overview

This protocol details the derivation of expandable skeletal myogenic progenitors (HEDEM/HIDEM) and multinucleated myotubes from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). The process involves reagent preparation, early commitment to a mesodermal lineage over one week, intermediate commitment with density adaptation, late commitment to high-density culture, and stabilization at passage zero. Myogenic differentiation is induced via lentiviral transduction of a tamoxifen-inducible MyoD1 construct followed by chemical activation and analysis via immunofluorescence for myosin heavy chain.

### Materials/Reagents

iPS cell medium, ES cell medium, Proliferation medium (including alternative if MegaCell DMEM unavailable), Feeder-free iPS cell medium, Commitment medium, Dissociation medium, Differentiation medium, Freezing medium, FACS buffer, Tween-20 (20% vol/vol), AP staining solution, 4-OH tamoxifen, Collagenase IV, 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde, Matrigel, Geltrex, Gelatin (EmbryoMax 0.1% wt/vol), Permeabilization buffer (0.2% vol/vol Triton/1% wt/vol BSA), Blocking buffer (10% vol/vol animal serum), Animal serum, Hoechst 33342, Hexadimethrine bromide (Polybrene), Trypan blue, Anti-MyHC primary antibody, Anti-mouse secondary antibody conjugated with fluorochrome, Fluorescence mounting medium.

### Equipment

0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters, 35-mm dishes, Six-well plates, 15-ml sterile tubes, P1000 pipette tips, Centrifuge, Incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, 3-5% O2), Microscope, Class 2 biosafety cabinet, Fluorescence microscope with 20× magnification lens (total 200×), Hot plate, Chemical cabinet.

### Safety & Sterility

Paraformaldehyde is extremely toxic; handle with adequate personal protective equipment under a chemical cabinet. Work involving viral vectors must be carried out under a Class 2 biosafety cabinet; appropriately inactivate residual lentiviral vector particles before disposal. AP staining solution is light-sensitive. Matrigel and Geltrex solidify above 4 °C; thaw on ice and use cold pipette tips. Do not keep cells in dissociation medium for more than 2 h total to maintain viability.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-experiment Setup

1. Prepare iPS cell medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare ES cell medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare proliferation medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. If MegaCell DMEM is not available, prepare an alternative proliferation medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare feeder-free iPS cell medium as specified in the accompanying table. Store it at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare commitment medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare dissociation medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare differentiation medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Prepare freezing medium as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the medium using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C protected from light for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Prepare FACS buffer as specified in the accompanying table. Filter-sterilize the buffer using 0.22-µm-pore vacuum filters and store it at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
11. Prepare 20% (vol/vol) Tween-20 by dissolving 2 ml of Tween-20 in 18 ml of double-distilled water. Store the solution at room temperature in a glass container for 1 month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
12. AP staining solution For each 35-mm dish to be stained for AP via enzymatic reaction, prepare 1 ml of staining solution by mixing 100 µl of 1 M Trizma hydrochloride, 100 µl of 1 M NaCl, 50 µl of 1 M MgCl2, 5 µl of 1 M Tween-20 (20% (vol/vol)), 725 µl of 1 M double-distilled water and 20 µl of 1 M NBT/BCIP stock solution. CAUTION The solution is light-sensitive. Always freshly prepare the staining solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S12 -->
13. Dissolve 4-OH tamoxifen powder in ethanol at a stock concentration of 25 mM and store aliquots at −20 °C for up to 1 month. Before use, thaw an aliquot, dilute it to 250 µM with PBS, and then dilute it 1:250 in fresh differentiation medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S13 -->
14. Dissolve collagenase in KnockOut DMEM at a final concentration of 1 mg/ml. Divide the solution into aliquots and store them at −20 °C for up to 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S14 -->
15. Dissolve 4 g of paraformaldehyde into 100 ml of PBS. Stir the solution on a hot plate and warm it to 60 °C. Adjust the pH to 7.4 by adding 1 N NaOH dropwise until the solution is completely clear. Adjust the final volume with double-distilled water. Divide the solution into aliquots and store them at −20 °C for up to 6 months. Once thawed, working aliquots can be stored at 4 °C for 1 week. CAUTION: Paraformaldehyde is extremely toxic and must be handled with adequate personal protective equipment under a chemical cabinet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S15 -->
16. Thaw an aliquot of Matrigel on ice. Once liquefied, dilute it to a 1:100 ratio in ice-cold DMEM using a cold pipette tip. Mix thoroughly and add 1 ml of the diluted Matrigel solution to each 35-mm dish or well of a six-well plate. Gently shake the plate to cover the entire surface with Matrigel. Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min, then remove residual Matrigel without scraping the bottom. For immediate use, plate cells in appropriate medium. For later use, cover the well with 1 ml of DMEM and return to the incubator at 37 °C. Coated plates should be used on the day of preparation. CRITICAL STEP: Undiluted Matrigel solidifies above 4 °C; therefore, thaw on ice and dilute in ice-cold medium with a cold pipette tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S16 -->
17. Thaw an aliquot of Geltrex on ice. Once liquefied, dilute it to a 1:100 ratio in ice-cold DMEM-F12 using a cold pipette tip. Mix thoroughly and add 1 ml of the diluted Geltrex solution to each 35-mm dish or well of a 6-well plate. Gently shake the plate to cover the entire surface with Geltrex. Incubate at 37 °C for 60 min, then remove Geltrex without scraping the bottom. For immediate use, plate cells in appropriate medium. For later use, wrap the plate with Parafilm and store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. CRITICAL STEP: Undiluted Geltrex solidifies above 4 °C; therefore, thaw on ice and dilute in ice-cold medium with a cold pipette tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S17 -->
18. Add 1.5 ml of EmbryoMax 0.1% (wt/vol) gelatin solution to each well of a six-well plate. Incubate at room temperature for 30 min. Discard the solution and immediately add cells resuspended in medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S18 -->
19. Prepare permeabilization buffer for immunofluorescence (0.2% vol/vol Triton/1% wt/vol BSA) by dissolving 1 g of BSA in 100 ml of PBS and stirring until dissolved. Add 200 µl of Triton X-100 and mix until dissolved. Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to 1 month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S19 -->
20. Prepare blocking buffer for immunofluorescence (10% vol/vol animal serum) by diluting 100 µl of animal serum in 900 µl of PBS (final volume 1 ml). Store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S20 -->
21. Thaw animal serum for immunofluorescence at 4 °C, divide into aliquots, and store at −20 °C according to the product's expiration date. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S21 -->
22. Dissolve Hoechst 33342 dye in water at a final concentration of 10 mg/ml. Divide the solution into aliquots and store protected from light at 4 °C for up to 6 months. Use this reagent diluted to a 1:250 ratio. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S22 -->
23. Prepare a stock solution of hexadimethrine bromide (Polybrene) at 8 mg/ml by dissolving the powder in sterile water. Store the solution protected from light at 4 °C for up to 1 year. Use it at a 1:1,000 dilution in proliferation medium when transducing cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S23 -->

## Early Commitment

### Day 0

1. Grow ES or iPS cell cultures to a confluency of approximately 70%, ideally starting with 1-3 wells of a six-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If any differentiated cells are present in the culture, manually select and remove them before starting the differentiation procedure. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
2. To increase single-cell survival after dissociation, pretreat the cells with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor by adding it to the cell culture medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
3. Remove the medium containing ROCK inhibitor from the plates and gently wash the cells with 2 ml of Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
4. Add 1 ml of prewarmed dissociation medium to each ES or iPS cell well and incubate at 37 °C for 10 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
5. Gently tap the side of the plates to facilitate colony dissociation and inspect for floating cells. If using feeder-dependent cultures, aim to detach most colonies while leaving feeder cells attached to the plastic. Since the first incubation is usually insufficient, return plates to the incubator and repeat tapping every 15 min for up to 2 h. Proceed when most colonies have detached as single cells or small clumps. Note: iPS cells cultured in feeder-free conditions detach easily, usually after 15 min at 37 °C, requiring no further incubation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not keep cells in dissociation medium for more than 2 h in total, as this decreases cell survival and compromises subsequent steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
6. Collect the dissociation medium containing detached cells into a 15-ml sterile tube. Gently resuspend the cells with a P1000 pipette tip to facilitate disaggregation of clumps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
7. Add at least 1 volume of prewarmed commitment medium to the tubes to dilute the dissociation medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
8. Centrifuge the cell suspension at 232g at room temperature for 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
9. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in prewarmed commitment medium, and count the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: To plate the appropriate number of cells, evaluate cell viability through vital staining, such as trypan blue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
10. Wash the Matrigel-coated dish twice with DMEM or PBS. Plate cells at 6 × 10^4 cells per cm^2 (~5 × 10^5 cells for a 35-mm dish if starting from feeder-dependent culture). If starting from feeder-free conditions, plate 3 × 10^5 cells per cm^2, corresponding to 2.5 × 10^6 cells for a 35-mm dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
11. Incubate the plate at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->

### Day 1

1. Replace the commitment medium the next day to eliminate dead cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Days 2-7

1. Inspect the plate daily and replace the commitment medium every 2-3 days with prewarmed fresh commitment medium. Refer to Figure 2 for representative cell morphology. Proceed to the next step after 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

## Intermediate Commitment

### Week 1

1. Prepare a 35-mm dish coated with 1% (vol/vol) growth factor-reduced Matrigel as described in the Equipment Setup section. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Dissociate the cell culture from Step 13 using prewarmed dissociation medium, as detailed in Steps 4-6. If cells do not detach completely after a maximum of 2 h in dissociation medium, perform additional gentle scraping of the dish surface. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. Collect the cells in dissociation medium into a 15-ml tube and gently resuspend them with a P1000 pipette tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Add 1 volume of prewarmed commitment medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
5. Filter the cell suspension through a 40-µm cell strainer placed on a collection tube to remove aggregates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
6. Centrifuge the filtered cell suspension at 232g for 5 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
7. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in prewarmed commitment medium, and count the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: To plate the appropriate number of cells, evaluate cell viability through vital staining, such as trypan blue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
8. Wash the Matrigel-coated dish twice with DMEM or PBS, and plate 2.5 × 10^4 cells per cm^2 (~2 × 10^5 cells for a 35-mm dish). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->
9. Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S10 -->
10. Inspect the plate daily and replace the commitment medium every other day with fresh prewarmed medium. Refer to Figure 2 for representative cell morphology. Proceed to the next step after 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S11 -->

## Late Commitment

### Week 2

1. Prepare a 35-mm dish coated with 1% (vol/vol) growth factor-reduced Matrigel as described in the Equipment Setup section. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Wash the plate with cells using 2 ml of PBS, then add 0.5 ml of trypsin to detach them. Incubate the plates at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2 for 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Remove plates from the incubator and shake to facilitate cell detachment. Inspect under a microscope. When all cells have detached, block trypsin activity with prewarmed commitment medium. Resuspend with a pipette and collect the cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the cell suspension at 232g for 5 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
5. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in prewarmed proliferation medium, and count the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: To plate the appropriate number of cells, evaluate cell viability through vital staining, such as staining with trypan blue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
6. Wash the Matrigel-coated dish twice with DMEM or PBS, and plate 2 × 10^4 cells per cm^2 (~1.6 × 10^5 cells for a 35-mm dish or at a confluence of 80%). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->
7. Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S08 -->
8. Inspect the cells daily and replace the medium every other day. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Proceed to the next step after 3 days at 100% confluence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S10 -->

## Culture Stabilization

### p0

1. Detach the cells by trypsinization as described in Steps 24 and 25. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the cell suspension at 232g for 5 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in prewarmed proliferation medium, and count the cells. Plate 1.2 × 10^4 cells per cm^2 on uncoated cell culture plastic. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
4. Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
5. Inspect the cells daily and split the culture by trypsinization as they reach 80% confluence. Different lines vary in proliferation rate, but generally require splitting every 3-4 days. This cell population is regarded as HEDEM/HIDEM passage zero (p0). From this point onward, cells are cultured similarly to bona fide mesoangioblasts and can be expanded and cryopreserved. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->

## Expansion and Cryopreservation

### at least 7-10 d

1. Split HEDEM and HIDEM cultures when they are roughly 80% confluent. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. On the day of splitting, wash the plates once with PBS, add the volume of trypsin necessary to cover the whole culture surface, and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Shake the plate to facilitate cell detachment and inspect under the microscope. When all cells are detached, add prewarmed proliferation medium to block trypsin activity. Resuspend and collect the cells in a tube for centrifugation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the cell suspension at 232g for 5 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->

## Myogenic Differentiation Induction

### 3 d after the first tamoxifen addition

1. Myotubes are usually identifiable in culture starting from 3 days after the first tamoxifen addition. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T1-S01 -->

### 6-7 d after the second tamoxifen administration

1. 6-7 days after the second tamoxifen administration and the switch to differentiation medium, the cell culture should be predominantly composed of multinucleated myotubes. These cultures are now ready to be analyzed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T2-S01 -->

### ~17 d

1. Induce myogenic differentiation via MyoD1 activation (Timing: ~17 days). Lentiviral transduction of HEDEMs/HIDEMs with MyoD-ER(T): Plate 1 × 10^5 HEDEMs or HIDEMs in a 35-mm dish in proliferation medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S01 -->
2. When cells are fully attached to the culture dish, thaw the MyoD-ER(T) lentiviral vector on ice and calculate the volume necessary to transduce cells with a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 1, 10, and 50. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: Work involving the use of viral vectors must be carried out under a Class 2 biosafety cabinet. Appropriately inactivate any residual lentiviral vector particles on surfaces and liquids that were in contact with it before their disposal. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Titrate the MOI to find the amount of lentiviral vector that allows the cell culture to differentiate into MyHC-positive myotubes with an efficiency >50%. Differentiation efficiency can be assessed only after transduction. We suggest performing experiments with cells that have the highest differentiation efficiency-to-MOI rate (i.e., the best differentiation with the lowest amount of lentiviral vector). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S04 -->
3. Dilute the lentiviral vector in 1 ml of proliferation medium supplemented with 1 µl of Polybrene. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S05 -->
4. Remove the medium from the 35-mm dish of MyoD-ER(T) HEDEMs or HIDEMs and replace it with 1 ml of viral suspension. Incubate the cells for 12 h at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S06 -->
5. Remove the medium and wash the plate twice with PBS. Add fresh proliferation medium to the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S07 -->
6. Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2 and inspect them daily. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S08 -->
7. Expand the cells as described in Steps 36-39. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B08-T0-S09 -->

## Differentiation Assay and Immunofluorescence

### Post-transduction

1. Prepare Matrigel-coated 35-mm dishes for differentiation assay and immunofluorescence for myosin heavy chain. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S01 -->
2. Plate 1.5-2 × 10^5 MyoD-ER(T) HEDEMs or HIDEMs on a Matrigel-coated dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S02 -->
3. Incubate the cells in growth medium at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 3-5% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S03 -->
4. Check the cells daily and add 1 mM 4-OH tamoxifen to the proliferation medium when the cells reach 90-100% confluence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S04 -->
5. After 24 h, replace the proliferation medium with fresh differentiation medium supplemented with 1 mM 4-OH-Tamoxifen. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S05 -->
6. Inspect the cultures daily for myotube formation. Replace half of the differentiation medium daily. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Differentiated cultures are delicate, as myotubes detach easily when plates are not handled gently. Medium change should be done slowly, and the medium should be added drop by drop on the side wall of the plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S07 -->
7. Wash the differentiated plate gently with PBS twice, and then fix it with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: Paraformaldehyde is extremely toxic and must be handled under a chemical cabinet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S09 -->
8. Permeabilize cells with PBS/0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100/1% (wt/vol) BSA for 30 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S10 -->
9. Remove the permeabilizing solution and incubate the cells with 10% (vol/vol) animal serum for 30 min at room temperature to block nonspecific binding sites. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S11 -->
10. Remove the animal serum and incubate the dish with anti-MyHC primary antibody for 1 h at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S12 -->
11. CRITICAL STEP: Another differentiated dish or a sector of the same dish needs to be incubated with secondary antibody and nuclear dye alone; this serves as a control to assess eventual nonspecific binding of the secondary antibody and evaluate background levels. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S13 -->
12. Perform three washes of 5 min with PBS/0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 to remove unbound antibody. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S14 -->
13. Incubate the dish with any anti-mouse secondary antibody conjugated with a fluorochrome of choice, diluted 1:500 in PBS/0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100/1% (wt/vol) BSA, at room temperature for 1 h. In the same incubation, counterstain the nuclei with a nuclear dye such as Hoechst (1:250). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S15 -->
14. Perform two washes of 5 min with PBS/0.2% (vol/vol) Triton to remove unbound antibody, and one wash of 5 min with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S16 -->
15. Carefully aspirate the last PBS wash from the dish and add one drop of fluorescence mounting medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S17 -->
16. Put a coverslip on top of the dish to protect the specimen and to avoid evaporation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S18 -->
17. Image the cells with a fluorescence microscope equipped with filters for the nuclear dye and the secondary antibody of choice. Take at least 10 random field pictures of the stained dish using a microscope equipped with a 20× magnification lens (total magnification 200×). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S19 -->
18. Merge nuclear dye images with MyHC images and count the total number of nuclei. Next, count only the number of nuclei localized within MyHC-positive myotubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S20 -->
